operator_io_quirks: All identifiers lowercase, no spaces; still double-quote in generated SQL.
Tiny tables (location 8, position 4, employee 25 rows) — no rowid sampling needed; original_values fully read.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes; only PKs (locationID, positionID, ssn) and two FKs employee->location/position.
Declared TEXT columns store money ('US$57,500.00'), dates ('10/1/04'), phone ('(404)333-5555'), SSN ('000-01-0000') — all dispatch to String fuzzer, not Date/Number.
hiredate is TEXT with M/D/YY format (no leading zeros, 2-digit year) — Date fuzzer never fires; String fuzzer will mangle it.
minsalary/maxsalary/salary TEXT with 'US$' prefix and comma thousands — String fuzzer's %-strip and int-like +-1 do not apply.
zipcode INTEGER but values like 2190 (leading-zero loss) — Number fuzzer fine, but zip semantics lost.
gender/performance have NULLs (0.04/0.08) though notnull=0; TS may or may not emit NULLs (String sampler drops None elements).
employee.lastname distinct 24 < 25 rows: one duplicate lastname — no unique constraint, so fine.
FKs point to existing, unique parents (locationID, positionID are PKs) — no dangling/non-unique FK issues.
No composite keys, no self-references, no views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs.
positionID/locationID in employee are INTEGER FK to INTEGER PK — Number fuzzer on parent, FK copy on child; consistent.
operator_ts_expectations: All TEXT columns -> String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0-20, plus 5 original samples, plus literal-pool values; contaminate 50%.
hiredate/salary/minsalary/maxsalary/ssn/officephone/zipcode-as-text get random garbage strings — implausible values drive FN on date/money/phone predicates.
INTEGER columns (locationID, positionID, zipcode, employee.positionID/locationID) -> Number fuzzer: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] with +-1/+-2 perturbation; PKs get fresh draws (max_l0=inf).
FK columns employee.positionID/locationID copy from parent's final filtered values with replacement — ties/duplicates likely, good for join tests.
PK dedup (sample_fresh_primary_keys) and unique dedup keep PKs distinct; ssn String fuzzer may collide but dedup drops repeats.
Table sizes: rand_lin ~30-230 or level-based (location/position level 0 small, employee level 1 x4) — tiny instances, few rows.
String fuzzer's int-like +-1 on '000-01-0000' etc. unlikely to parse as int; %-strip no-op (no % in samples).
NULLs: String sampler drops None elements, so gender/performance NULLs likely absent in generated rows — misses IS NULL tests (FN).
Date fuzzer never used (no date/timestamp declared type) — hiredate comparisons on '10/1/04' style will mostly fail to match generated strings.
Number fuzzer on zipcode produces values outside 5-digit range — zip predicates implausible (FN).
Literal pool from train SQL may inject real city/state/title strings into String sampler, partially rescuing plausibility.
